correctness.rationale: No pair dominates since each closed neighborhood has seven vertices. The independently reconstructed minimum family consists of the 32 triples in the two stated translation orbits. A one-vertex exchange between independent dominating sets is a slide: the new set must dominate the removed vertex, and no unchanged vertex was adjacent to it, so the arrival vertex is adjacent to it. In coordinates, the cross-orbit overlap shifts are D={(0,0),(1,2),(3,1)} with no two-vertex overlaps within an orbit. The triangles are the 32 stated faces and each primal edge is in two faces. The displayed linear map has unit determinant and sends D to D'={(0,0),(0,3),(1,0)}, proving the graph isomorphism. The separately written /workspace/branches/409e5724-a412-4f41-9e56-88ea883e24de/independent_structural_check.py reconstructed all 32 and 48 masks matching the frozen certificate and independently checked the map and all-source distances (1,3,6,9,9,4). Analytically, two steps within a part project to Cayley differences D'-D' minus zero, exactly the standard Shrikhande connection set C, so the even levels have sizes 1,6,9. D' reaches three vertices at distance one and D'+C reaches twelve distinct vertices including those three, giving nine at distance three. The remaining four are at distance five because the even part is exhausted within four steps. Translation and part swap with coordinate negation give the same layers from every start. The frozen verifiers were inspected, not executed.
